name: a_ai_platforms
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: AI platforms & disruption.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Consumer and enterprise AI product launches (agents, models, devices), adoption metrics, big-tech event announcements; analyst notes naming stocks that win or lose from these launches (disruption baskets, second-order beneficiaries) with the stock moves.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **MDB** — Software & SaaS
- MongoDB CEO Chirantan Desai resigned with immediate effect on October 2 to lead a new AI initiative at Meta; former CEO Dev Ittycheria returned as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. MongoDB shares were reported down about 14.7% for the week as of October 2; Stifel’s Brad Reback reiterated **Buy** with a **$465** price target. (Investing.com, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 08:52 ET)
- Meta’s consumer rollout of **Muse**, described as an autonomous web-navigating AI agent, was cited in connection with Desai’s move to Meta. (Investing.com, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 08:52 ET)

## **META**, **OPENAI**, **ASANA**, **MNDY**, **BL**, **DBX**, **HUBS**, **INTU**, **PAYC**, **PCTY**, **ZM** — Software & SaaS
- Bank of America analysts led by Tal Liani identified **Asana, monday.com, BlackLine, Dropbox, HubSpot, Intuit, Paycom, Paylocity and Zoom** as software companies potentially exposed to disruption from consumer and small-business AI agents; the note cited Meta’s **Muse** and OpenAI’s **Dots** as examples of agents that could handle simpler workflows directly. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2 17:04 ET)
- Bank of America identified **CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle** as potential beneficiaries of higher inference and computing demand from wider agentic-AI adoption. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2 17:04 ET)

## **SNPS** — Semiconductor IP / AI Infrastructure
- Synopsys announced a partnership with OpenAI to develop **GPT-Synopsys**, a specialized model for chip design, and a multiyear intellectual-property agreement with Amazon for custom-silicon collaboration. Synopsys shares were reported up **12.8% on October 1** and about **9.2% for the week** as of October 2; StoneX analyst Gary Mobley reiterated **Buy** with a **$570** price target. (Investing.com, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 08:52 ET)

## **HPE** — AI Infrastructure
- Daiwa upgraded Hewlett Packard Enterprise to **Outperform** from **Neutral** and set a **$75** price target on October 2. (247WallSt, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 09:17 ET)
- A separate October 2 analyst roundup reported that Truist, Piper Sandler and Wells Fargo raised HPE price targets on networking and AI, while Evercore moved to **In Line** on valuation; the available report did not provide each firm’s old and new target. (Investing.com, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 11:13 ET)

## **CSCO** — Communications & Networking
- Cisco shares rose **3.2% to $112.20** on October 2; the report cited Zacks’ upgrade from **Hold** to **Strong Buy**, fiscal-fourth-quarter 2026 product-order growth of **35% year over year**, and a sovereign-AI infrastructure partnership with Bell Canada. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 08:01 ET)
- Piper Sandler lowered Cisco’s price target to **$125**; the report stated that AI represented about **6% of fiscal-2026 revenue**. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 08:01 ET)

## **CBRS** — AI Compute
- Freedom Capital upgraded Cerebras Systems to **Buy** from **Hold** and set a **$209** price target on October 2. (247WallSt, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 09:17 ET)

## **AAPL** — Internet & Platforms
- Morgan Stanley lowered Apple’s price target to **$355 from $360** while retaining an **Overweight** rating; the report cited potential disruption to Apple’s services business if AI agents such as Meta’s Muse bypass the App Store. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; latest update available Oct. 5 06:28 ET)

## **SpaceXSI / xAI** — AI Platforms
- Elon Musk said on October 4 that SpaceX’s AI unit would be renamed **SpaceXSI**; the report stated that no implementation date or additional details were provided, so the item is **[rumor]** regarding timing and corporate implementation. (Reuters, as reported by IndMoney, Oct. 5 09:21 ET)
- The same report stated that **Grok 4.7** API availability had been dated September 21, with a **500,000-token context window** for coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work; this background predates the requested window. (IndMoney, latest update Oct. 5 10:00 ET)
- SpaceX stock was reported at **$158.96 on October 2**, up approximately **7.35%** in that regular session; the report did not identify a US-listed public ticker. (IndMoney, latest update Oct. 5 10:00 ET)
